title.narrative: Effective Stabilization in Conflict Zones: Central African Republic, Ethiopia and Mozambique

description.narrative: Stabilization programmes have been deployed to restore a sense of normalcy, enabling returns, preventing protracted displacement, breaking the reliance on protracted humanitarian cycles and laying the foundations for recovery, peace and development. This funding window allocation, in line with the UNDP stabilization approach, will support the scaling up of stabilization in Central African Republic, Ethiopia and Mozambique. In Central African Republic, it will support the scale-up of the stabilization programme and the strategic geographic extension of the programme in the Ouham prefecture of CAR, which shares a border with Chad. In Ethiopia, UNDP advances stabilization through the Peace-Support Facility (PSP), it will prioritize rapid response initiatives in three key woredas: Tehuledere and Habru in Amhara, and Hawzen in Tigray. In Mozambique, it will initiate stabilization in southern Cabo Delgado, in districts such as Ancuabe, Chiure and Meluco, where the NSAGs have escalated their attacks. Finally, the Crisis Bureau will provide backstopping support for effective stabilization by pre-positioning capacity to offer technical support and accompaniment, information systems for real data collection and analysis and learning processes to enhance preparedness, informed/evidence-based decision making and maximize opportunities for scalability and replicability of future stabilization interventions.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
